spark.scene: True-color satellite view of the main Hawaiian Islands from northwest to southeast heavily obscured by thick white cumulus and cirrus clouds over dark ocean. Island landmasses are partially visible through breaks, with the large island in the southeast largely covered by dense white cloud. No distinct gray, brown, or bluish haze or linear plume distinguishable from ordinary clouds is visible.

kilauea.activity_summary: Kīlauea volcano is intermittently erupting short, precursory lava flows continuing the activity that began September 7. The forecast window for onset of episode 55 fountaining is now September 10-11 given no change in summit inflation since yesterday. Overview: Kīlauea volcano has been intermittently erupting lava flows from the north vent in Halemaʻumaʻu since September 7.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts increased in August, while the summit region showed no other signs of deformation. Mauna Loa had an increase in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 87 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the August reporting period, after 57 in July. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
